definitions.explanation: The process of training animals, especially horses, to follow commands and behave in desired ways. The standard term in horse racing and animal handling.
Used informally or humorously to describe strictly training or disciplining a person, often implying a power dynamic.

examples.japanese: {馬|うま}を{調教|ちょうきょう}する。
この{犬|いぬ}はよく{調教|ちょうきょう}されている。
{調教師|ちょうきょうし}が{毎朝|まいあさ}{競走馬|きょうそうば}の{調教|ちょうきょう}を{行|おこな}っている。
examples.english: The trainer conducts training of the racehorses every morning.

examples.japanese: {新人|しんじん}を{調教|ちょうきょう}する。
examples.english: To whip the newcomer into shape.

examples.japanese: {先輩|せんぱい}に{厳|きび}しく{調教|ちょうきょう}された。
examples.english: I was strictly trained by my senior.

examples.japanese: うちの{部長|ぶちょう}は{新人|しんじん}の{調教|ちょうきょう}に{定評|ていひょう}がある。
examples.english: Our department head has a reputation for training newcomers well.

notes:
Primarily used for animal training, especially in horse racing where {調教師|ちょうきょうし} (trainer) is an official title. When applied to people, it carries a humorous or ironic tone, implying strict discipline similar to animal training.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {調教師|ちょうきょうし}: animal trainer (especially horse racing)
- {調教|ちょうきょう}を{受|う}ける: to undergo training
- {調教|ちょうきょう}が{行|い}き{届|とど}いている: to be well trained
- {調教|ちょうきょう}する: to train/tame

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {訓練|くんれん}: training — general purpose, for people or military
- しつけ: discipline — for children or pets, upbringing
- {飼|か}い{慣|な}らす: to domesticate — focuses on the taming process
